description: Wispr Flow is offered to every user in the picker with no way to know whether the org has API access; the only handling is a gray 'API access required' line, which in the mockup appears with no attempt made.
expected: Do not offer Flow, or show the message only after Connect fails.
suggested_fix: Decide the access signal (catalog flag) in S1b.

description: Transcription row shows 'Wispr Flow' as soon as it is picked, before a key is verified; in the blocked state it still reads Wispr Flow although calls cannot use it.
expected: Row keeps the old value until the key verifies.
suggested_fix: Draw row as 'Not connected' or keep previous value until Connect succeeds.

description: Key field placeholder is the generic 'API key', the same label the voice providers use; it does not name Wispr Flow.
No Verifying and no Key rejected state on mobile; web draws both.
'API access required' is 13 px neutral gray, not destructive color.
Red Disconnect has no confirmation drawn. Native iOS uses an alert or action sheet for destructive actions; plan is silent.
'This device' (On) and 'Transcription' sit together with no stated precedence; story MB-6 shows the call plan ignores Transcription when This device is on.
expected: One control or a stated rule.

description: Providers list labels each 'Speak + transcribe' or 'Speak only'; Flow is transcribe-only and fits neither.
suggested_fix: Add wording or keep Flow out of this list (it is).
